title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-06-23
content:
Perf Benchmarking Sync - 2026-06-23
Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Marco Ruiz, Jing Wei, Tom Harris, SRE rotation (on-call)
Duration: 45m
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime

Agenda:
- Quick recap of last week's regressions
- Review latest test runs (bench-run-2026-06-23-01)
- Triage suspected root causes (kernel selection, batching, KV cache)
- Action items and owners

Summary:
We observed a p95 latency regression and a drop in sustained throughput on the nightly benchmarks after the 2026-06-20 roll (PR #789 merged). Canary traffic showed increased tail latency for medium-length requests (seq_len 512). The regression appears reproducible on A100 80GB nodes with the redwood-v1-7b-quant profile when using the new fused-attn kernel.

Key findings from test runs:
- Environment: nightly bench cluster (A100 80GB, CUDA 12.2, torch-nightly build), model: redwood-v1-7b-quant, compile flags: -O2 + fused-attn enabled
- Benchmark run: bench-run-2026-06-23-01, steady-state load for 30m, mixed seq lengths (64/128/512), client QPS ramp to 1200rps
- Baseline (pre-PR #789, 2026-06-19): p50=18ms, p95=78ms, throughput=1200 rps sustained
- Current (post-PR #789): p50=20ms (+11%), p95=132ms (+69%), throughput dropped to 950 rps (-21%)
- Regression surface: p95 increases mainly on seq_len=512 and when batcher queues are non-empty (bursty traffic). p50 impact is modest.

What we tried so far:
- Rolled back fused-attn kernel via local toggle: reverting kernel selection to legacy reduced p95 back to ~82ms (close to baseline).
- Increased batcher max_batch_size from 32->48: slightly improved throughput but worsened p95 (more queuing).
- Disabled continuous-prefetch optimization: no meaningful change.
- KV cache hit-rates unchanged (cache policy not implicated).

Hypothesis:
- Fused-attn kernel optimization introduces worse tail behavior under mixed sequence-length workloads due to variable per-sample runtimes and the way we schedule micro-batches onto SMs. When batcher queues are non-empty, the scheduler groups heterogenous lengths, causing head-of-line blocking and higher p95. The legacy kernel, while slightly slower single-sample, has more predictable per-sample latency which reduces tail.

Short repro steps for engineers:
1) Checkout commit range: master@{2026-06-18}..master@{2026-06-21} (includes PR #789).
2) Run bench harness: tools/bench/run.py --env=nightly-a100 --model=redwood-v1-7b-quant --seq-distribution="64:0.5,128:0.3,512:0.2" --duration=1800 --ramp=600 --batcher-max=32
3) Toggle fused-attn via env var: RW_KERNEL=fused-attn vs RW_KERNEL=legacy
4) Collect traces: grafana dashboard link in linked_artifacts

Open tickets and links:
- INF-4721: investigate fused-attn tail regression (P0)
- PR #789: fused-attn kernel selection change (suspected)
- bench-run-2026-06-23-01: raw metrics and artifacts in S3

Decisions made in meeting:
- Short-term: temporarily disable fused-attn kernel for the hosted fleet canary and nightly jobs until we have a fix (rollback window agreed).
- Mid-term: implement scheduler-aware batching (group by seq_len buckets before batching) as a mitigation; target prototype in 2 sprints.
- Long-term: collaborate with kernel authors to make fused-attn preemptible or add per-sample timeout estimation for better scheduling.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Aisha: Open emergency revert PR to toggle fused-attn off by default for hosted-canary (due 2026-06-24) [blocked by CI flakiness - Marco to help]
- Marco: Bisect commit range and confirm minimal repro commit (due 2026-06-24) [Jing to assist with bench harness logs]
- Jing: Prototype seq_len bucketing in batcher (in-branch) and run microbenchmarks (due 2026-07-07)
- Tom (SRE): Apply toggle to hosted canary and monitor Grafana for p95 over next 48h (due 2026-06-25)
- All: Add more detailed perf traces to bench harness (include CUDA kernel timings) and attach to INF-4721 (due 2026-06-30)

Notes / thoughts / parking lot:
- Need to check if quantization changes interact with fused-attn (quantized load patterns could change memory access characteristics).
- Consider adding per-request seq_len histogram to APM traces to better correlate tail spikes with traffic mix.
- There may be a scheduling bug in the CUDA kernel that only emerges at certain concurrency levels; need kernel-level profiling.

Follow-ups planned:
- Short sync scheduled: 2026-06-24 10:00 PT (15m) to confirm revert status and initial metrics after toggle.
- Deep dive: 2026-06-29 1h workshop with kernel authors + infra to review flamegraphs and CUDA traces.

Appendix: Quick log snippets (from bench-run-2026-06-23-01)
- "p95 132ms @ 14:12:03, seq_len=512, active_batches=18"
- "GPU utilization steady ~62%, but per-SM utilization variance high"
- "CUDA kernel A fused-attn runtime skew: mean 0.8ms, stdev 1.9ms (heavy tail)"

If you have additional experiments to propose, paste them in this doc or ping @aisha in Slack.

-- Aisha
